story.head: Patience vs. spray-and-pray
paras: The Sabres (11-11-4) lost 6-3 to Pittsburgh on Friday, and the Flames (11-14-2) lost 5-3 to New Jersey the same night. Going in, the Sabres are sixth in the Atlantic (tied for 19th in the NHL) and the Flames sixth in the Pacific (24th).
This season, the Sabres have been outscored 89-81, even though they’ve outscored teams 57-55 at 5-on-5. On special teams, opponents have outscored them 25-15.

The Sabres rarely get pinned in their own end (3rd) and get their defensemen shooting (5th), but don’t block many shots (30th). As for the Flames, they play some of the league’s fastest games (2nd) and have struggled on the power play (32nd). They also take a lot of low-quality shots (32nd), so the Sabres wait for good looks, but they settle for hopeful ones. Calgary has scored 2.59 goals a game, the third fewest in the league. Something has to give when the Flames’ shooting runs into the Sabres’ defense.

Tage Thompson (17 G / 14 A / 31 P in 26 GP) leads the Sabres in scoring, with eight points in his last five games and a point in six straight games against Calgary. Jack Quinn (14 G / 12 A / 26 P in 26 GP) is next in line, with seven points in his last five games. For the Flames, Joel Farabee (8 G / 13 A / 21 P in 27 GP) leads the way in scoring, and Matt Coronato (7 G / 12 A / 19 P in 27 GP) isn’t far behind.
Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen (8-5-3 / .877 SV% in 15 GS) will likely start for Buffalo, and Dustin Wolf (6-6-2 / .878 SV% in 14 GS) for Calgary.
